title: Mary Oliver's birth chart
metaDescription: Mary Oliver's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 17.0° Virgo. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Mars and Pluto sit 0.8° from an exact trine — near enough that the tradition reads drive and depth as a single working part. Trines are read as inheritance rather than achievement: the ease is genuine, and nothing about it was earned.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's exact place is 17.0° Virgo. That falls in the second decan, 10°–20°, sub-ruled by Saturn in the classical scheme — a earth sign read through a mutable season.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Closer in, Mercury stands at 10.5° Libra; Venus stands at 13.3° Virgo; Mars stands at 26.1° Scorpio. The tradition reads a mind at home in argument and pattern from Mercury, taste for the substantial and the lasting from Venus, drive that moves on certainty and current from Mars.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Nothing in the geometry sits closer than Mars and Pluto: 0.8° from an exact trine. Trines are read as inheritance rather than achievement: the ease is genuine, and nothing about it was earned. Behind it, Saturn sextile Uranus at 0.9°, and Venus conjunction Neptune at 1.1° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has two entries for this chart. Venus in Virgo at 13.3° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Mars in Scorpio at 26.1° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 4 earth, 4 water, 2 air by element and 4 mutable, 4 fixed, 2 cardinal by modality. Earth signs hold the scheme’s slow end, where results are measured in what survives rather than what starts. No settled placement falls in fire — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Venus, Saturn and Uranus were retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Aquarius for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 14.9° between midnight and midnight. That is quick enough to make the exact degree a neighbourhood rather than an address, and slow enough to leave the sign settled. At the noon reference it stands at 16.1°.
